# Locality Guide: Zhydivska Hreblia, Tarashcha Uezd, Kyiv Guberniya, Russian Empire (1840–1900)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Village:** Zhydivska Hreblia (Жидівська Гребля); Soviet-era name Chapaievka; modern name Kalynove (Bila Tserkva Raion, Kyiv Oblast, Ukraine)
- **Uezd (county):** Tarashcha Uezd
- **Guberniya (province):** Kiev (Kyiv) Governorate, Russian Empire
- **Formed:** Kiev Governorate was created in 1796 from the Kiev Viceroyalty, per Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiev_Governorate). It comprised 12 uyezds and was abolished in 1923–1925 by Soviet administrative reforms.
- **Administrative center:** Tarashcha (the uezd seat)
- **Population during period:** Population data not returned for this specific place by the population tool.
- **Economy:** Predominantly agrarian; peasant smallholding and estate agriculture typical of Right-Bank Ukraine in the 19th century.
- **Ethnic composition:** Primarily Ukrainian Orthodox peasants; some Polish Catholic gentry and Jews in the broader uezd.
- **Religious denominations:** Russian Orthodox (dominant); Roman Catholic (Polish gentry); Jewish; smaller numbers of Greek Catholic unlikely in this part of Kiev Governorate (Greek Catholic was more prevalent in Galicia/western Ukraine).
- **Key historical events:** Emancipation of serfs in 1861 (affecting record-keeping and mobility of peasant population); institution of universal conscription in 1874.

## Boundary changes
- The village remained within Tarashcha Uezd, Kiev Governorate throughout the target period (1840–1900) — no boundary changes split records across jurisdictions during this window.
- Before 1796, the territory was part of the Kiev Viceroyalty; records from before that date would be sought under the earlier jurisdictional structure.
- After 1923, Soviet administrative reform abolished the old uezd structure. The territory passed through Bila Tserkva Okrug (1923–1930), then became part of Kyiv Oblast. Modern records are held at the State Archive of Kyiv Oblast.
- The village's modern name (Kalynove) and Soviet name (Chapaievka) do not appear in any 19th-century records; always search under Zhydivska Hreblia or its Cyrillic form.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** Civil registration in Ukraine began in 1920 at the state level, per the FamilySearch Wiki ([Ukraine Civil Registration](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ukraine_Civil_Registration)). No civil vital registration exists for the 1840–1900 period.
- **What exists:** None for this period.
- **Pre-registration source:** Orthodox church metrical books (see Church records below) served as the de facto vital record system throughout 1840–1900.

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Russian Orthodox (primary for Ukrainian peasant population). Roman Catholic records may exist for Polish gentry families. Jewish metrical books are separate.
- **Record types:** Births/baptisms, marriages, deaths/burials. Printed forms in a standardized three-column format were introduced in 1806; a revised format introduced in 1838 prevailed until 1920. Per the [Ukraine Church Records wiki page](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ukraine_Church_Records), coverage reached approximately 90% of the Orthodox population after 1800.
- **Where held (originals):** Central State Historical Archives of Ukraine (TsDIAU), Kyiv, holds the Kyiv Consistory duplicates.
- **Primary online collection:** **Ukraine, Kyiv, Orthodox Consistory Church Book Duplicates, 1723–1931** at FamilySearch ([collection 1503045](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1503045)) — indexed + images, free. Also available on Ancestry (subscription: https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/62358/). The collection covers Kyiv, Zhytomyr, Vinnytsia, and Cherkasy oblasts (the former Kiev Governorate area). Records are in Russian (Cyrillic). The volume_search for Tarashcha, Kiev Governorate, 1840–1900 returned 1,944 matched digitized volumes, all previewed volumes having 100% name-indexing. Only the leading results were inspected in this survey; 1,944 is the full count returned by the tool.
- **Burial register content:** Per the wiki, death/burial entries may give: name, date and place of death or burial, age, residence, cause of death, names of survivors (especially a widow or widower), father's name, and deceased's birth date and place.
- **Confession lists (supplementary):** **Ukraine, Kyiv, Confession Lists, 1741–1934** ([collection 2290980](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/2290980)) — partial index + images, free. These annual household lists record family members attending Easter confession, giving names, ages, and household relationships. Useful for establishing family composition when the exact death year is unknown. 51 million records, 40,448 images.
- **Language:** Russian (Cyrillic). The [Russian Genealogical Word List](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Russian_Genealogical_Word_List) and [Russia Handwriting guide](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Russia_Handwriting) will be needed to read originals.

### Census records
- **Revision lists (the closest equivalent to a census before 1897):** The Russian Empire conducted ten revisions (household tax enumerations) sporadically from 1719 to 1858. Those overlapping the target period: 8th revision (1833–1835), 9th revision (1850–1851), 10th revision (1857–1858). Per the [Ukraine Census wiki page](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ukraine_Census), revision lists record name, parentage, age, social rank, relationship to household head, and notes on deaths since the previous revision. Coverage approximately 75% of the taxable population; clergy, nobility, military, and foreigners are excluded. Revision lists were NOT compiled for non-taxed classes.
- **Where held:** State archives. Revision lists appear on FamilySearch under the uezd name — search the FamilySearch Catalog at https://www.familysearch.org/search/catalog under 'Tarashcha, Kiev Governorate, Russian Empire' and look under Taxation or Census categories.
- **Online access:** MyHeritage has an index of [Ukraine, Revision Lists, 1795–1904](https://www.myheritage.com/research/collection-20234/ukraine-revision-lists) (subscription). The FamilySearch Catalog for Tarashcha returned results but full enumeration was not possible in this survey due to output size; search the catalog directly.
- **Family lists (post-1861):** Local population enumerations conducted from approximately 1860–1920, not universally mandated. They exist randomly and identify about 30% of the population. Check the State Archive of Kyiv Oblast and the FamilySearch Catalog.
- **1897 Russian Empire Census:** The only general census of the Russian Empire was conducted January 28, 1897. Many returns were destroyed after statistical processing. Check the [Altai State University map project](https://arch1897.histcensus.asu.ru/) to see if Tarashcha Uezd returns survived. The [Ukraine, Odessa, Census, 1897](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/2380520) on FamilySearch covers only Odessa — no Kiev Governorate equivalent was found in the collections search.
- **Access:** Revision lists largely browse-only (unindexed images) unless an index exists in the Catalog; MyHeritage index is subscription-only.

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Wills, administrations, guardianships, inventories, estate distributions. For a peasant family in 1840–1900, formal probate was uncommon; property typically passed by customary practice.
- **Where held:** Uezd-level court records would be at the State Archive of Kyiv Oblast. The FamilySearch Catalog for this place may include court records; search directly under Tarashcha, Kiev Governorate.
- **No dedicated FamilySearch online collection** was found for Tarashcha court/probate records in this survey.

### Land records
- **Survey system:** Russia used a mix of allodial estate registers and communal peasant land allotments (after the 1861 emancipation). Deeds and land grants for estate holders were maintained at the provincial level.
- **Land-distribution jurisdiction:** The Kiev Governorate land office (Kyiv) would hold estate records. After emancipation, local land reform boards (uezd-level) administered peasant allotments.
- **Types:** Deed registers, land survey maps, allotment records post-1861.
- **Where held:** State Archive of Kyiv Oblast and TsDIAU. The [Ukraine Land and Property wiki page](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ukraine_Land_and_Property) returned minimal content — no specific collections for Kiev Governorate were listed. No dedicated online collection was found in this survey.

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts:** Crimean War (1853–1856); Russo-Turkish War (1877–1878); universal conscription instituted 1874 (Alexander II).
- **Record types:** Recruit/conscription lists (from 1874), military service records, pension files.
- **Conscription lists:** Per the [Ukraine Research Tips wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ukraine_Research_Tips_and_Strategies), conscription lists begin in 1874. A man born ~1818 would have been beyond typical conscription age in 1874, but his sons would appear. These records are held at state archives.
- **Online:** No dedicated FamilySearch collection for Tarashcha military records was found in this survey. The pra.in.ua database (https://pra.in.ua/) indexes some military records from 1650–1920 (incomplete, free).

### Cemetery records
- **Major cemeteries:** Village cemeteries (Orthodox church grounds) associated with the parish serving Zhydivska Hreblia. Specific cemetery names were not returned by any tool in this survey — the neighboring-parishes table was not available because the Tarashcha home wiki page did not exist.
- **Online coverage:** No specific FindAGrave or BillionGraves coverage for this village was confirmed in the external links.
- **Physical records:** Sexton and burial registers (if any) would be part of the parish records now held at TsDIAU.

### Immigration/emigration records
- **Context:** Emigration from Kiev Governorate to the United States increased notably after the 1880s. Hamburg Passenger Lists (1850–1934) are available at Ancestry (https://search.ancestry.com/search/db.aspx?dbid=1068). Naturalization records were filed at local U.S. courts and are held at NARA or state archives.
- **Relevant collections (from external_links_search):** Hamburg Passenger Lists 1850–1934 (Ancestry); Russians Immigrating to the US 1834–1897 (MyHeritage, subscription); Immigrants from the Russian Empire at Library and Archives Canada 1898–1922.
- **Note:** For the 1840–1900 period, emigration from this specific village is uncertain but possible post-1880s. Declarations of intention and naturalizations were filed inland at U.S. courts if the family emigrated.

### Tax records
- **Types:** Poll tax (soul tax) records underpin the revision lists (see Census records above). After 1861 emancipation, land redemption payments created local tax records.
- **Value:** The 10th revision (1857–1858) would record Grigory Kokosha (born ~1818) as a household head or member; the revision notes those who died between revisions, which could bracket his death.
- **Where held:** State archives, under Tarashcha Uezd.

### Newspaper records
- **Local papers:** No specific local newspaper for Tarashcha Uezd was identified in the survey. Regional papers existed in Kyiv.
- **Online access:** The [Ukraine Newspaper Search at Ukrainian Weekly](http://www.ukrweekly.com/uwwp/archive/) (1933–2014) is far later than the target period.
- **Content value for this period:** Not a primary source for 1840–1900 village-level research.

### Other record types
- **Confession lists** (covered under Church records above) are a second-tier source for family composition.

# Locality Guide: Zhydivska Hreblia, Tarashcha Uezd, Kyiv Guberniya, Russian Empire (1840-1900)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Village:** Zhydivska Hreblia (historical); Soviet-era name Chapaievka; modern name Kalynove, Bila Tserkva Raion, Kyiv Oblast, Ukraine
- **Uezd (county):** Tarashcha Uezd
- **Guberniya (province):** Kiev (Kyiv) Governorate, Russian Empire
- **Formed:** Kiev Governorate created in 1796 from the Kiev Viceroyalty (Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiev_Governorate). It comprised 12 uyezds and was abolished by Soviet reform in 1923-1925.
- **Administrative center:** Tarashcha
- **Economy:** Predominantly agrarian; peasant smallholding and estate agriculture typical of Right-Bank Ukraine.
- **Ethnic composition:** Primarily Ukrainian Orthodox peasants; Polish Catholic gentry and Jews present in the broader uezd.
- **Religious denominations:** Russian Orthodox (dominant for Ukrainian peasants); Roman Catholic (Polish gentry); Jewish.
- **Key events:** Emancipation of serfs 1861; universal conscription introduced 1874.

## Boundary changes
- The village remained within Tarashcha Uezd, Kiev Governorate throughout 1840-1900 with no boundary splits during this window.
- Before 1796 the territory was part of the Kiev Viceroyalty; records from before 1796 would be sought under that earlier jurisdiction.
- After 1923, Soviet reform divided Kiev Governorate into okrugs; the territory passed through Bila Tserkva Okrug and eventually became part of modern Kyiv Oblast.
- The village's modern name (Kalynove) and Soviet name (Chapaievka) do not appear in any 19th-century records.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** Civil registration in Ukraine began in 1920 at the state (Soviet) level, per the [Ukraine Civil Registration wiki page](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ukraine_Civil_Registration). No civil vital registration exists for the 1840-1900 period.
- **Pre-registration alternative:** Orthodox church metrical books served as the de facto vital record system for baptisms, marriages, and deaths/burials throughout 1840-1900.

### Church records
- **Denominations:** Russian Orthodox (primary for Ukrainian peasant population). Roman Catholic records exist for Polish gentry families. Jewish metrical books are filed separately.
- **Metrical book format:** Per the [Ukraine Church Records wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ukraine_Church_Records), printed forms were introduced in 1806; a revised three-column format introduced in 1838 prevailed until 1920. Coverage reached approximately 90% of the Orthodox population after 1800.
- **PRIMARY COLLECTION (indexed + images):** [Ukraine, Kyiv, Orthodox Consistory Church Book Duplicates, 1723-1931](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1503045) at FamilySearch (collection 1503045) - 12.8 million records, 29.4 million persons, 2.1 million images - free. Also available on Ancestry (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/62358/) by subscription. The collection covers parishes in the former Kiev Governorate (now Kyiv, Zhytomyr, Vinnytsia, and Cherkasy oblasts). Records are in Russian (Cyrillic). Originals are held at the Central State Historical Archives of Ukraine (TsDIAU), Kyiv.
- **Volume search count:** 1,944 digitized volumes matched Tarashcha, Kiev Governorate, Russian Empire for 1840-1900. All previewed volumes showed 100% name-indexing (searchable by name) and language: Russian. Only the leading results were inspected in this survey.
- **Burial register content:** Per the wiki, a death/burial entry may include: name and age of the deceased, date and place of death, date and place of burial, cause of death, names of survivors (especially widow/widower), father's name, and the deceased's place of residence.
- **Confession lists (supplementary):** [Ukraine, Kyiv, Confession Lists, 1741-1934](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/2290980) at FamilySearch (collection 2290980) - 51 million records, 40,448 images - partial index + images, free. Annual household lists recording family members attending Easter confession; useful for bracketing a death year by presence/absence.
- **Language:** Russian (Cyrillic). See the [Russian Genealogical Word List](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Russian_Genealogical_Word_List) and [Russia Handwriting guide](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Russia_Handwriting).

### Census records
- **Revision lists (closest equivalent to census, 1719-1858):** Ten household tax enumerations were conducted sporadically. Those overlapping the research window: 8th revision (1833-1835), 9th revision (1850-1851), 10th revision (1857-1858). Per the [Ukraine Census wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ukraine_Census), they record name, parentage, age, social rank, household relationship, and notes on persons who died between revisions. Coverage approximately 75% of the taxable population; clergy, nobility, military, and foreigners are excluded.
- **Where to find revision lists:** Search the FamilySearch Catalog at https://www.familysearch.org/search/catalog under 'Tarashcha, Kiev Governorate, Russian Empire' in the Taxation or Census categories. Revision lists appear under the uezd name. MyHeritage has an index of [Ukraine, Revision Lists, 1795-1904](https://www.myheritage.com/research/collection-20234/ukraine-revision-lists) (subscription).
- **Family lists (post-1861):** Local population enumerations conducted approximately 1860-1920, not universally mandated. They identify about 30% of the population and are found in state archives.
- **1897 Russian Empire Census:** The only general census was taken January 28, 1897. Many returns were destroyed after statistical use. Check whether Tarashcha Uezd returns survived at the [Altai State University map project](https://arch1897.histcensus.asu.ru/).
- **Access level:** Revision lists are largely browse-only (unindexed) unless specifically indexed in the Catalog; the MyHeritage index requires a subscription.

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Wills, administrations, guardianships, inventories. For a peasant in 1840-1900, formal probate was uncommon.
- **Where held:** Uezd-level court records are at the State Archive of Kyiv Oblast. No dedicated FamilySearch online collection for Tarashcha court records was found in this survey.

### Land records
- **Survey system:** Russian Empire metes-and-bounds estate records; communal peasant allotments after 1861 emancipation.
- **Where held:** Kiev Governorate land office records are at TsDIAU and the State Archive of Kyiv Oblast. The [Ukraine Land and Property wiki page](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ukraine_Land_and_Property) returned minimal content and listed no specific collections for Kiev Governorate. No dedicated online collection was found in this survey.

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts:** Crimean War (1853-1856); Russo-Turkish War (1877-1878); universal conscription from 1874.
- **Record types:** Conscription lists (from 1874), military service records. A man born ~1818 would be beyond conscription age after 1874, but his sons would appear.
- **Online access:** The pra.in.ua database (https://pra.in.ua/) includes some military records, 1650-1920, free but incomplete. No dedicated FamilySearch collection for Tarashcha military records was found.

### Cemetery records
- **Type:** Village Orthodox church cemetery records associated with the parish serving Zhydivska Hreblia.
- **Online:** No specific FindAGrave or BillionGraves coverage for this village was confirmed.
- **Physical:** Sexton and burial registers are part of the parish records now at TsDIAU.

### Immigration/emigration records
- **Context:** Emigration from Kiev Governorate to America increased after the 1880s. Hamburg Passenger Lists 1850-1934 are at Ancestry (https://search.ancestry.com/search/db.aspx?dbid=1068). Naturalization records for emigrants are at U.S. court archives.
- **Declarations of intention and naturalizations** were filed inland at U.S. courts and are searchable via NARA.

### Tax records
- **Types:** Poll tax (soul tax) records underpin the revision lists. After 1861, land redemption payment records were created.
- **Practical value:** The 10th revision (1857-1858) would record Grigory Kokosha and note if he died before the next revision; the 9th revision (1850-1851) establishes him alive at that date. These can bracket the death year.

### Other record types
- **Database of Ukrainian residents (pra.in.ua):** Free, incomplete index of birth registers, fiscal and parish censuses, lists of nobility, voters, military, and victims of repressions, 1650-1920 (https://pra.in.ua/).
- **Kiev Gubernia Gazetteer (Spiski Mest, 1901):** Lists settlements with administrative context. Available at https://www.familysearch.org/library/books/records/item/573037-spisok-naselennykh-mest-kievskoi-gubernii.

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | Ukraine, Kyiv, Orthodox Consistory Church Book Duplicates, 1723-1931 (collection 1503045) - indexed + images | Free |
| FamilySearch | Ukraine, Kyiv, Confession Lists, 1741-1934 (collection 2290980) - partial index + images | Free |
| Ancestry | Kyiv, Ukraine, Orthodox Consistory Church Book Duplicates, 1734-1930 | Subscription |
| MyHeritage | Ukraine, Revision Lists, 1795-1904 - indexed | Subscription |
| pra.in.ua | Database of Ukrainian residents, 1650-1920 - partial index | Free |

**Coverage of this survey:** The volume search returned 1,944 digitized volumes matching Tarashcha, Kiev Governorate, Russian Empire for 1840-1900. Only a preview of the leading results was examined; all previewed volumes showed 100% name-indexing.

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Central State Historical Archives of Ukraine (TsDIAU), Kyiv | Original Orthodox metrical books (consistory duplicates); administrative records | In-person or written request; http://www.archives.gov.ua/Eng/ |
| State Archive of Kyiv Oblast | Revision lists, family lists, post-1920 civil registration, land records, court records | In-person or written request |
| Regional State Archives (general) | Oblast-level contacts at https://old.archives.gov.ua/Eng/Archives/regional.php | |

## Records NOT online
- Kiev Governorate revision lists (may exist as microfilm in the FamilySearch Catalog; no dedicated indexed online collection comparable to the Zaporizhia revision-list collection was found)
- Land records, deed registers, estate books
- Court and probate records
- Conscription lists
- 1897 census returns for Tarashcha Uezd (survival unconfirmed)

## Known record losses
- Church records in Ukraine were centralized in government archives rather than systematically destroyed in the Soviet period, per the [Ukraine Church Records wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ukraine_Church_Records). However, destruction of active churches in the 1930s means post-1930 parish-level records are often absent.
- The 1897 census Ministry copy was destroyed after statistical processing. Local copies may survive.
- No specific courthouse fires or record destructions for Tarashcha Uezd were identified in this survey.

## Research tips
- **Search by name first.** The Kyiv Orthodox Consistory Church Book Duplicates (collection 1503045) are 100% name-indexed. Search for the surname Kokosh/Kokosha in Cyrillic (Кокоша) at https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1503045. See: [collection guide](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ukraine,_Kyiv,_Orthodox_Consistory_Church_Book_Duplicates_-_FamilySearch_Historical_Records).
- **Browse by place if the index is incomplete.** Browse: Province (Kiev) > District (Tarashcha) > Parish/Village > Year > Death. All parishes in Tarashcha Uezd are filed together per year, so browse the Tarashcha volumes for the likely death window if a name search misses anything.
- **Use revision lists to bracket the death year.** The 9th (1850-1851) and 10th (1857-1858) revisions should record Grigory as a household member if living; notes on deaths between revisions may directly state when he died. Search the FamilySearch Catalog under 'Tarashcha, Kiev Governorate, Russian Empire' in Taxation/Census. [Ukraine Census wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ukraine_Census).
- **Use confession lists as a secondary bracket.** Collection 2290980 lists families annually for Easter confession. Grigory's absence from a year's list, after appearing in prior years, narrows the death window.
- **Always search under the historical village name.** Use Zhydivska Hreblia (Жидівська Гребля or variant spellings) when browsing images. Soviet-era name (Chapaievka) and modern name (Kalynove) will not appear in 19th-century records.
- **Records are in Russian (Cyrillic).** The post-1838 death column layout typically shows: name and age, date of death, date of burial, cause of death, officiating priest. [Russian Genealogical Word List](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Russian_Genealogical_Word_List); [Russia Handwriting guide](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Russia_Handwriting).
- **Check the FamilySearch Catalog** for microfilmed revision lists and any additional church volumes: https://www.familysearch.org/search/catalog, place 'Tarashcha, Kiev Governorate, Russian Empire'. The catalog returned results in this survey but individual titles could not be fully enumerated due to output size.
- **Tutorial:** The RootsTech session 'Research in Eastern Ukraine using Russian Empire Records' (https://www.familysearch.org/rootstech/session/research-in-eastern-ukraine-using-russian-empire-records) demonstrates navigating FamilySearch images and the catalog for metrical books and revision lists.
- **For records not yet online,** contact TsDIAU (http://www.archives.gov.ua/Eng/) or the State Archive of Kyiv Oblast. A Russian-language letter-writing guide is at https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Russian_Letter_Writing_Guide.

entry.exhaustive_search_summary: Research addressed the two primary digital repositories for 19th-century Tarashcha uezd vital records. FamilySearch collection 1503045 (Ukraine, Kyiv, Orthodox Consistory Church Book Duplicates, 1723-1931) was searched in multiple passes covering both surname forms Кокоша and Кокошенко, including a FAN search for the widow Татьяна Гейко/Кокоша; the 1846 death register entry (src_001) was found and confirmed from the original image (log_032). Collection 2290980 (Ukraine, Kyiv, Confession Lists, 1741-1934) was searched in multiple passes with year and place filters, yielding the 1821 household record (src_002). Full-text search across all FamilySearch-indexed collections returned no results due to Cyrillic corpus coverage gaps. Revision list holdings for Tarashcha uezd (9th revision 1850-1851, 10th revision 1857-1858) were sought via FamilySearch Catalog and record search; no digitised holdings were confirmed — physical copies at the State Archive of Kyiv Oblast are beyond digital tool reach. The original Orthodox metrical books at the Central State Historical Archives of Ukraine (TsDIAU), Kyiv, were not accessed; collection 1503045 holds contemporaneous consistory duplicates of the same records and answered the question without requiring the physical originals. Both unsearched record classes (revision lists and TsDIAU originals) would corroborate the established death date and place but would not narrow the specific finding of 18 September 1846.
entry.narrative_markdown:
## Proof Summary: Death of Григорий Захаров Кокоша

**Research question:** When and where did Григорий Захаров Кокоша (born about 1818 in Zhydivska Hreblia, Tarashcha, Kiev, married Татьяна Иванова Гейко in 1843) die?

**Conclusion:** The evidence strongly suggests that Григорий Захаров Кокоша died on 18 September 1846 in the village of Жидовская Гребля (Zhydivska Hreblia), Tarashcha uezd, Kyiv guberniya, Russian Empire, of natural causes, and was buried on 20 September 1846 at the Иоанно-Богословская (St. John the Theologian) parish church. This conclusion is assessed as probable.

### Primary Evidence: 1846 Death Register

The foundation of this conclusion is a death register entry for Жидовская Гребля, recorded in the books of the Иоанно-Богословская church for 1846 and preserved in the Kyiv Orthodox Consistory church book duplicates on FamilySearch. The entry records Григорий Кокоша, economic peasant, who died 18 September 1846, age 25, of natural causes, and was buried 20 September 1846; certifying priest Романъ Вишневскiй. The entry was confirmed directly from the original image (log_032).[^1]

This record is classified as an **original record** — the consistory duplicate is a contemporary copy made at the time of registration, not an index derived later. For the death date and place, the information is **primary**: the certifying priest acted in his official capacity at the event, making him the firsthand recorder of the death rather than a secondary reporter. The reported age (25, implying a birth year of about 1821) is **secondary information** supplied by a family informant not personally present as a witness, and carries correspondingly less weight. The priestly attestation of the death on 18 September 1846 in Жидовская Гребля therefore carries the highest evidentiary value available for a pre-civil-registration Ukrainian village death.

No patronymic appears in the deceased's name column for this entry. The record is silent on the father's name rather than contradicting the tree's "Захаров."

[^1]: "Україна, дуплікати метричних книг Київської Православної консисторії, 1723-1931", *FamilySearch* (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:KX55-44K : Mon Dec 01 11:02:07 UTC 2025), Entry for Григорий Кокоша, 18 Sep 1846.

### Identity Corroboration: 1821 Confession List

A record from a wholly separate source — the 1821 Kyiv Governorate confession list in FamilySearch collection 2290980 — records Григорий Захарович Кокоша, age 3, as a child in the household of Захарий Иванович Кокоша.[^2] This is an **original record** of a different type (a periodic ecclesiastical confession enumeration, not a vital register), from a different collection, recorded 25 years before the death register, by a different informant. It independently establishes:

- The full given name Григорий and the surname Кокоша
- The patronymic Захарович, confirming the father as Захар — consistent with tree person GST7-TS8 (Захар Иванов Кокошенко) and the tree's "Захаров" designation
- A birth year of about 1818 (age 3 in 1821), consistent with the tree
- The family structure, consistent with the tree's recorded siblings (sister Мария Захариевна, born about 1814; sister Катерина Захариевна, born about 1820)

For the biographical data, this confession list yields **indeterminate information** — the household informant is unknown and proximity cannot be assessed. For the fact of residence and census presence, the information is **primary** (the enumerator visited the dwelling).

The coincidence of an identical given name and the relatively rare surname Кокоша in the same village, with a named father matching the tree and ages spanning a 25-year interval in the same locality, makes it virtually certain that the Григорий Захарович Кокоша of the 1821 confession list and the Григорий Кокоша of the 1846 death register are the same individual and the subject of this question.

[^2]: "Украина, Киевские исповедные ведомости 1741-1934", *FamilySearch* (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:6263-HLN7 : Tue Jul 09 03:51:47 UTC 2024), Entry for Захарий Иванович Кокоша and Анастасия Кокоша, 1821.

### Birth Year Discrepancy

The death register implies a birth year of about 1821 (from the reported age of 25 at death in September 1846), while the 1821 confession list implies a birth year of about 1818 (age 3 in 1821). This three-year gap is a noted discrepancy. The confession list figure is more reliable: it was recorded approximately three years after the birth, while the death register age was reported by a family informant not present as a witness, some 25 or more years after the birth. Three-year disparities of this kind are common in pre-civil-registration Ukrainian Orthodox records, where informants gave approximate rather than registered ages. This discrepancy concerns the birth year — a collateral biographical fact — and does not affect the target facts of this question: the death date and death place, which rest on primary information from the certifying official. The discrepancy does not alter the identity conclusion or the death conclusion.

### Temporal Consistency

An existing tree fact (Birth, id e19c486d, Zhydivska Hreblia, 1844) for Григорий's daughter Анна (tree person GW7Y-SYS) establishes that Григорий was alive as a parent as late as 1844. Fact e19c486d carries no linked source entry in research.json; it was contributed through FamilySearch Tree user submissions (person-level source references Q68H-RHW and Q68H-RXQ on GW7Y-SYS). The death date of 18 September 1846 falls approximately two and a half years after this last confirmed living date and is temporally consistent.

### Research Scope and Limitations

FamilySearch collection 1503045 (Ukraine, Kyiv, Orthodox Consistory Church Book Duplicates, 1723-1931) was searched in multiple passes covering surname forms Кокоша and Кокошенко, including a FAN search for the widow Татьяна Гейко/Кокоша; the 1846 death register entry was found and confirmed from the original image. Collection 2290980 (Ukraine, Kyiv, Confession Lists, 1741-1934) was searched in multiple passes with year and place filters. Full-text search across all FamilySearch-indexed collections returned no results due to Cyrillic corpus coverage gaps. Revision list holdings for Tarashcha uezd (9th revision 1850-1851, 10th revision 1857-1858) were sought via FamilySearch Catalog and record search; no digitised holdings were confirmed — physical copies at the State Archive of Kyiv Oblast are not digitally accessible. The original Orthodox metrical books at the Central State Historical Archives of Ukraine (TsDIAU), Kyiv, were not accessed; collection 1503045 holds contemporaneous consistory duplicates of the same records, which answered the question. Both unsearched record classes would corroborate the established death date and place but would not narrow the specific finding.

The conclusion is assessed as **probable** rather than proved because only one original source directly attests the death event with primary information; a second independent source with primary information for the death itself was not found among the digitally accessible records. The two unsearched classes of records (revision lists and TsDIAU originals) are beyond digital tool reach and would at most corroborate, not change, this finding.

## Result

**Григорий Захаров Кокоша died on 18 September 1846 in Жидовская Гребля (Zhydivska Hreblia), Tarashcha uezd, Kyiv Guberniya** — now Kalynove, Kyiv Oblast, Ukraine. He was buried two days later at the Иоанно-Богословская (St. John the Theologian) parish church. Age recorded at death: 25. Cause: natural.

### Evidence assembled (GPS tier: **Probable**)

| Source | Record | Role |
|--------|--------|------|
| **src_001** `ark:/61903/1:1:KX55-44K` | Death register, 18 Sep 1846 — Иоанно-Богословская church, Жидовская Гребля; original image confirmed (log_032) | **Primary / direct** evidence for the death event |
| **src_002** `ark:/61903/1:1:6263-HLNH` | 1821 confession list — *Григорий Захарович Кокоша*, age 3, b. 1818, son of Захарий Иванович Кокоша; confirms patronymic and family | Identity corroboration; independent record type and informant |
| **src_003** `ark:/61903/1:1:6N3N-CQ81` | 1840 confession list — *Татиана Иоаннова Гейко*, b. 1823, Popruzhna | Corroborates wife's identity |

### Why "probable" rather than "proved"
The GPS requires two independent sources attesting to the *death fact itself*. A second direct death attestation (a widow-listing confession entry, or a revision-list noting him deceased) could not be found digitally: indexed 1840s confession lists for Zhydivska Hreblia parish are absent from FamilySearch, Tarashcha revision lists have no digitised holdings, and the Cyrillic records are not yet in the full-text corpus. The only path to "proved" is through the physical holdings at the State Archive of Kyiv Oblast (revision lists) or TsDIAU. The identity match is strong — exact surname and given name, exact same village, patronymic confirmed by the 1821 confession list — and no contradictory evidence was found in any searched repository.

### Note on birth year
The death record's recorded age (25) implies birth ~1821; the 1821 confession list establishes birth ~1818. A three-year discrepancy is routine for estimated ages in 19th-century Ukrainian Orthodox death registers. It does not affect the death conclusion.
